_colour_legend: Kept identical across all four styles so the plates read as one poster, and deliberately echoing the CDC PHIL #10708 colorized TEM (violet particles on warm orange): VP1 P-domain arches = soft violet / lilac protein; the 32 cup-shaped hollows between them = deeper indigo shadowed pits; S (shell) domain beneath = muted sea-green / teal even layer; single (+)ssRNA genome inside = one continuous coppery-orange thread; VP2 minor protein = one small dusty plum lobe on the inner shell face. Colour is a teaching convention - virions are colourless and TEM is greyscale.
textbook: Clean cutaway TEXTBOOK ILLUSTRATION of a SINGLE norovirus particle (family Caliciviridae, the tiny non-enveloped gut virus behind the winter vomiting bug), centered in a square 1:1 1080x1080 frame with generous empty negative space around it for later labels. HOUSE STYLE, match it exactly: a refined, elegant scientific-textbook diagram - semi-flat vector-like shading, THIN clean dark outlines (never heavy black cartoon strokes), gentle soft shading with subtle dimensionality, and a MUTED, sophisticated, slightly desaturated educational palette of soft dusty tints. Never bright, never primary, never candy-coloured, never glossy plastic, never a cartoon. Every structure gets its own distinct soft colour fill so a reader can tell them apart. Neutral dark charcoal uncluttered background filling the frame edge-to-edge - no border, no frame, no vignette, no letterbox. Draw the virion as a THREE-DIMENSIONAL ball seen at a slight angle (not a flat circular cross-section diagram): the intact outer surface covers most of it, and a single WIDE WEDGE - a full quarter of the ball - has been lifted out of the front to open a deep hollow bowl, exactly like a cut-away model. Not a thin slit, not a narrow slot, not an equatorial band. The particle is NAKED and NON-ENVELOPED and has only ONE protein capsid layer. THE SURFACE IS THE MOST IMPORTANT PART OF THIS IMAGE - GET IT RIGHT BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE. The capsid is ONE single moulded protein shell whose own surface is buckled into relief. NOTHING is glued, stuck, pinned or mounted on top of it, and no small separate emblems, marks or motifs are scattered over it. The overall silhouette stays a clean, believable SPHERE - gently bumpy, but not a lumpy potato and not an irregular blob. (a) RAISED ARCHES: about ninety low, broad, rounded ridges swell up OUT OF the shell. Each ridge is made of TWO rounded protein lobes side by side, leaning together and merging along their tops, so each looks like a tiny stone bridge, a croissant lying on its side, or two thumbs pressed together under a sheet of rubber. They are part of the shell and grow smoothly out of it with no visible join, no base plate and no socket. Each rises only about one twelfth of the ball's diameter and is much WIDER THAN IT IS TALL. FORBIDDEN SHAPES for these raised features: a stalk, a stem, a neck, a waist, a pin, a rivet, a cotton reel, a drawing pin, a mushroom, a trumpet or funnel mouth, a golf tee, a cone, a pyramid, a triangular stud, a ball on a stick, a club, a knob on a stalk, a spike, a horn, a tentacle, a ray, a hair, a raised tube or chimney with a lip, and - most important - any X shape, cross, plus sign, bowtie, star, asterisk, letter or symbol. IF ANY SURFACE FEATURE HAS A NARROW WAIST BENEATH A WIDER TOP, OR LOOKS LIKE A LITTLE OBJECT SITTING ON THE BALL, THE IMAGE IS WRONG. (b) SUNKEN CUPS: between and around the arches the shell is scooped out into THIRTY-TWO large round CRATERS. Each crater is a genuine three-dimensional EXCAVATION with visible sloping inner walls and a dark shadowed floor at the bottom - like a thumb pressed deep into soft clay, or a dimple in a golf ball. FORBIDDEN for these hollows: a flat painted circle, a flat disc, a ring, a donut, a target, a concentric ring, a spot, a dot, a porthole, an eye, a raised collar or rim standing proud of the surface, or any purely two-dimensional marking. They must be sunk INTO the shell with real depth and real shadow. Twelve craters sit at the twelve pointed vertices of the icosahedron and twenty at the centres of its twenty triangular faces, so only about TWELVE TO FOURTEEN are visible on the near side - keep them few, large and deep rather than many and small. These cups are why the whole virus family is named after the Latin word for a drinking cup, so they must be unmistakable. The finished ball must read as KNOBBLY, PITTED and DIMPLED - never a smooth featureless bead, never a spiky sea urchin, never a starburst, never a crown of studs, never a mass of tubes. Colour the raised arches soft dusty violet and lilac, and shade the insides of the craters deep muted indigo so their depth reads clearly. Along the cut edge, show that the arches sit on a CONTINUOUS, EVEN, MUTED SEA-GREEN INNER SHELL of uniform thickness - ONE single layer only, never two and never three - which encloses the hollow interior. Inside the hollow interior lies ONE SINGLE UNPAIRED THREAD of coppery-orange RNA, loosely and IRREGULARLY coiled and folded back on itself like a length of soft cooked spaghetti or a carelessly dropped piece of string, loosely filling part of the cavity with uneven, natural, non-repeating loops. It is a SINGLE strand. FORBIDDEN: two strands twisted around each other, a double helix, a twisted ladder, drawn base-pair rungs, a regular corkscrew or spring, a tidy geometric spiral, a figure-of-eight, a woven basket, a neatly wound ball of yarn, a neat maze or circuit-board pattern, several separate rods or segments, and beads on a string. Beside it sits exactly ONE small dusty-plum lobe resting against the inner face of the shell. Do NOT draw any lipid envelope, membrane bilayer, glycoprotein fringe or fuzzy halo of any kind - norovirus is NON-ENVELOPED, and drawing a membrane is the single worst error. Do NOT draw long club-shaped or mushroom-headed coronavirus spikes, stalked knobs, thin rays, sunbeams or hairs; do NOT draw a smooth featureless sphere with no craters; do NOT draw a second or a third concentric shell nested inside the first (multiple nested layers belong to rotavirus and are WRONG here - there is exactly ONE capsid shell); do NOT draw a segmented or double-stranded genome; do NOT draw a helical, rod-shaped or bullet-shaped capsid; no phage tail, base plate or legs; no cell organelles; no face, eyes or limbs. Anatomically faithful, one specimen only, structures well separated so labels can attach. The image must contain ZERO writing of any kind: no letters, no words, no numbers, no protein names such as VP1, VP2, P1, P2 or S, no captions, no labels, no legend, no arrows, no scale bar, no signature and no watermark anywhere in the picture.
